questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a totally different culture, as well as new ways to experience university life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We received informative emails about everything we needed to know, so it was very easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were all given a "buddy" we could contact if we had any questions about anything. A buddy is basically a korean student who will help you throughout the semester if you need anything. We also had introductory courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find. The university supplied a websites where we could find accommodation, and there are a lot to choose from.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living close to the university. They have a lot of student housing options close to campus which is really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is a first come first served process, so you need to be quick if you want specific courses. There was a period where we could choose our preferred courses and thereafter a period where we were able to pick your final ones. The first week of the semester, we could swap out courses if we needed to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received a document were everything was detailed with important dates and so on.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was semi successful, i got a few classes i wanted but i should have chosen more, so i could try a bunch of courses and then drop the courses i didn't find interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend researching each course your find somewhat interesting and read through the syllabus provided for the course. Then choose many courses so you have a few backups if you aren't able to get the courses you wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of the courses to be quite easy, however, i had to spend a lot of time studying.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was very different compared to UCPH. I had two courses that heavily focused on discussions where the professor would act as a mediator or a discussion facilitator.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Programming for Policy Informatics
Theories of Media Effects
Entertainment and Strategic Communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Entertainment and Strategic communication as our professor was very kind and a good at creating useful discussions. I also liked getting tangible skills or tools for strategic communication.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not really have any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I did not expected produce, like fruits and vegetables, to be so expensive, which is why i rarely cooked any food myself.
Eating at restaurants or fast food places in general is quite cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs, however, there were a lot of social activities available that i did. They had a lot of pop op events or small concerts. I do know however that there are a lot of different clubs available to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend trying all the different restaurants and cafes that are available, as well visiting other cities around the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Jeju Island and Busan are good destinations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, as the people are very friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would attend a lot the social activities and events that are held during the semester, as well as just being friendly and respectful when talking to the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find any cultural differences that challengin.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How social people are. People are frequently out eating dinner, drinking together and enjoying each others company which was probably my favorite part of their culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Attend as many social activities as possible, soak in the city and don't be afraid to try new things and make mistakes or even ask your fellow student for help if you need to.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get familiar with the campus as it might be confusing to find the locations of each class.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Completing my courses and feeling like a left the country with a lot valuable experiences both personally and academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably living by myself, as i have been used to living with other people my whole life. However, there are a few places that offer social living which i have heard was pretty good.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
